hook: Nunes Won the Fight She *Gave Away*
dek: Amanda Nunes hurt Kayla Harrison on the feet, then chose to grapple with her instead.

slides.label: Round 1
slides.text: Nunes came out swinging, stunned Harrison and nearly finished her. The *comeback looked real*.

slides.label: The Pivot
slides.text: Then Harrison scored a *takedown*. Nunes ended the round on her back, first of many.

slides.label: Round 2
slides.text: Nunes stayed in the clinch instead of breaking away, chasing a *takedown of her own*.

slides.label: The Throw
slides.text: Harrison answered with a *judo throw*, put her down again, worked the crucifix till the horn.

slides.label: Round 3
slides.text: Nunes doubled down, even took Harrison's back, but she turned it, *mounted*, and opened a cut.

slides.label: Round 4
slides.text: Spent, Nunes threw a kick. Harrison caught it, took her back and closed the *choke in seconds*.

slides.label: The Verdict
slides.text: Rear-naked choke, 1:29 of round four. Harrison keeps the title. *Worst. Gameplan. Ever.*

slides.label: The Lesson
slides.text: Nunes had the *one thing* Harrison couldn't match, and set it down to prove she could win the other way.

cta_line: *Strength you don't use is not strength*
question: Did Nunes lose it, or did Harrison take it?
first_comment: Harrison had spinal fusion surgery in January, this was her first fight back in 18 months. Still earned Performance of the Night.

caption_instagram:
Kayla Harrison vs Amanda Nunes was supposed to be a statement comeback at UFC 334, and for most of round one, it was. Nunes hurt Harrison on the feet, stunned her, almost finished her. That was the blueprint: stand, strike, make the judoka walk through fire for a grip.

Then Nunes put the blueprint down. She chased takedowns against a two time Olympic judo champion, ate throws, got mounted, got cut. By round four she was spent, threw a kick, and Harrison caught it, took her back, and closed a rear naked choke at 1:29 to keep the title.

Give Harrison everything, she's 20-1 and fighting for the first time in 18 months after spinal fusion surgery. But the lesson belongs to Nunes: strength you don't use is not strength.

Did Nunes lose it, or did Harrison take it?

caption_linkedin:
At UFC 334, Amanda Nunes had the clearest edge of the fight, and she set it down anyway.

She hurt Kayla Harrison on the feet early, stunned her, nearly finished her. Then, instead of staying in her lane, Nunes chose to grapple with a two time Olympic judo champion, on the champion's terms. Round after round she ate takedowns, got mounted, got cut, and by round four she was spent enough that Harrison caught a kick, took her back, and closed a rear naked choke to keep the title.

Harrison earned every bit of it, fighting for the first time in 18 months after spinal fusion surgery. But the lesson that travels outside the cage belongs to Nunes: strength you don't use is not strength, it's a story you tell yourself.

Every founder has an edge they stop using the moment they want to prove they can win the other way.

Did Nunes lose it, or did Harrison take it?
